preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or have gained ownership through the vulnerability)
Contract must have ETH balance > 0 (from accumulated fees or direct transfers)

exploit_hint: The contract has two low-level calls without return value checks in swapBack() and withdrawStuckETH(). If the ETH transfer fails (e.g., operationsAddress is a contract with fallback that reverts), funds remain locked. However, the owner can change operationsAddress to a malicious contract that always fails transfers, then use withdrawStuckETH() which also doesn't check return value. This allows the owner to drain ETH by: 1. Set operationsAddress to a contract that always reverts on receive, 2. Let ETH accumulate from fees, 3. Call withdrawStuckETH() - the call will succeed even if ETH transfer fails, but owner can make the recipient contract successfully receive funds while appearing to fail.
